messages.subject: "w" matrix  and CAR interpretation
parts:
I am a little bit confused with hoe I should calibrate and use the "w" matrix within a poisson model in brms. Here is my model below:
I have a two levels model,  "mat" is the matrix generated for the first level (is that correct to do so?). The intention was to control the spatial autocorrolation at that level. The second level is comprised within the dataset and it is named "UPPERGEOG".




model <- brm(Y ~ relevel(SES1, ref= "Q1") + relevel(SES2, ref="Q1") + (1|UPPERGEOG)+ offset(log(EXP)), data = DATASET,family="poisson", control = list(max_treedepth = 35), autocor=cor_car(mat, type= ("escar")), prior=PriorBrFullLasso,warmup = 4000, iter =25000, chains= 6)



My second question is about the einterpretation of the car and sdcar correlation structure. I have no idea how to interpret those:




Group-Level Effects: 
~LGA (Number of levels: 16) 
              Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
sd(Intercept)     0.05      0.02     0.02     0.09       5073 1.00

Correlation Structure: car(mat, ~1, 'escar')
      Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
car       0.98      0.02     0.92     1.00       1555 1.01
sdcar     0.17      0.01     0.15     0.18       7289 1.00

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] "w" matrix and CAR interpretation
parts:
I would use the adjacency matrix of the level with the higher (more detailed) spatial resolution. For your data, your approach seems reasonable to me.

If you want to learn more abour CAR models, please consider reading the block post of Max Joseph at https://github.com/mbjoseph/CARstan.
